title: Tiered local response with Needle3 and LFM2.5

claims.text: nvsh answers routine operator requests and routine failures locally in well under a second: a tiny Needle3 reflex picks a typed deterministic operation, a small resident LFM2.5 agent handles the middle ground, and the configured full agent is called only when neither can — so even a Jetson Orin Nano gets a useful nvsh with no large model at all.

honesty_conditions.text: On an Orin Nano with no full agent configured, a fast-path prompt from the corpus produces a correct proposal, and a should-escalate prompt produces a plain 'no local answer and no full agent configured' message rather than a guess.

claims.text: Operators working at a bash prompt on NVIDIA edge and desktop machines where a large model is slow, remote or absent — first of all a Jetson Orin Nano (8 GB unified memory), then AGX Orin, AGX Thor and DGX Spark — plus the nvsh maintainers who must benchmark each tier before promoting it.

honesty_conditions.text: The benchmark is actually run on an Orin Nano, an AGX Orin, an AGX Thor and a DGX Spark, and each device's results file is committed; a device that was not measured is listed as not measured.

claims.text: Every request nvsh cannot answer from a slash command goes to one configured NvshAgent harness (pi, qwen, claude, codex, ...). A plain request like 'how hot is this machine' or 'restart vllm' pays a full agent turn — seconds to tens of seconds, and a network hop when the model is on another box — and a machine with no reachable large model gets no agent help at all.

honesty_conditions.text: A timing of the same fast-path prompt through today's default full agent is recorded on at least one device, so the 'before' cost is a measured number and not an estimate.

claims.text: Most operator asks and many failures are routine: they map to one of a small set of deterministic operations. Answering those locally in milliseconds makes nvsh feel like a shell feature instead of a chat round-trip, keeps air-gapped Jetsons useful, and saves the full agent for problems that need reasoning.

honesty_conditions.text: The corpus run reports what share of requests were answered below Tier 3; if that share is small the results say so.

claims.text: The local tiers are packaged with nvsh as optional install flavors (extras in the `nvsh[...]` form) and run on the operator's own machine; they are not wired through the lobes gateway or any other model server on the network, because each model is small enough to live beside nvsh.

nvsh has proper telemetry, logging, observability and metrics for the tiered path, so the system can be measured and improved: every request records which tier answered, what it selected, its confidence, its latency, whether it escalated and why, and what the operator then did with the proposal.

honesty_conditions.text: One nvsh command prints per-tier counts, latency percentiles, escalation reasons and operator approve/decline rates from local records, with `--json`; every record passes through the existing redactor, and the raw request text is stored only when the operator has opted in.

claims.text: A request or qualifying failure goes through tiers in order: Tier 0 shell and slash commands, Tier 1 Needle3 selecting one typed operation, Tier 2 a small resident LFM2.5 agent running a bounded inspect-interpret-propose loop, Tier 3 the configured full NvshAgent. Each tier either answers with a normal nvsh Proposal or declines, and a decline moves the request up one tier. A machine with only Tier 1 (or Tiers 1-2) installed is a supported configuration, not a degraded one.

honesty_conditions.text: A test drives one request through each path with fixture tiers — answered at Tier 1, declined by 1 and answered at 2, declined by both and answered at 3 — and asserts that the audit log names the tier and the decline reason each time.

claims.text: nvsh gains a typed operation table — the deterministic operator tools the issues assume but the code does not have yet. Each operation has a name, typed arguments, a read-only or mutating flag, and a per-platform implementation that renders to a concrete command (through `jetson-cli` / `dgx-spark-cli` / `rtx-spark-cli` when installed, plain system tools otherwise). The first table covers at least: `device_info`, `system_stats`, `gpu_stats`, `power_get`, `power_set`, `service_status`, `service_restart`, `service_logs`, `docker_list`, `docker_restart`, `process_list`, `nvsh_doctor`. One table serves all tiers and all four device classes.

honesty_conditions.text: Every operation in the table has a table test per platform kind asserting the exact rendered command, and an argument that could inject shell syntax (a service named `x; rm -rf /`) is refused by validation.

claims.text: A local tier never executes anything and never emits a free-form shell string. It returns an operation name plus arguments; nvsh validates both against the operation table, renders the command itself, and hands the result to the existing approve/execute/verify loop as a normal `Proposal`. An unknown operation, an argument that fails validation, or a runtime error is a decline, never a guess. nvsh calls Needle's select-only `complete()` and never its executing `run()`.

honesty_conditions.text: A test gives a fixture tier output naming an unknown operation, a bad argument and a raw shell string, and all three become declines; a grep-style test asserts nvsh's needle adapter never references `Needle.run`.

claims.text: Confidence is recorded but is not the safety mechanism. A read-only operation selected by a tier may be proposed directly; a mutating operation selected by a tier always shows the operator the interpreted operation and arguments and needs approval exactly as today. Thresholds for declining are configuration, tuned from measured data, and the design works for a fine-tuned Needle model that reports no confidence at all.

honesty_conditions.text: A test with a fixture tier returning a wrong mutating operation at confidence 1.0 shows the interpreted operation in the panel and executes nothing without approval; the same flow passes with confidence set to None.

claims.text: Tier 1 and Tier 2 ship as optional flavors (`nvsh[needle]`, `nvsh[lfm]`, and a combined one); `dependencies = []` stays empty, the hook and every existing verb work unchanged when no flavor is installed or a flavor's runtime is broken, and no tier code is imported on the success path or at hook time.

honesty_conditions.text: CI installs the wheel with no extras and runs the full suite and the import-time test; a test with a deliberately broken flavor import shows the request reaching the full agent with one status line.

claims.text: The tiers work fully offline once prefetched: an explicit nvsh command downloads the engine and model files ahead of time, reports where they are and how big, and after that no tier makes a network call. Third-party telemetry in a bundled runtime is switched off by nvsh (`NEEDLE_TELEMETRY=0`, `DO_NOT_TRACK=1`) before the runtime loads.

honesty_conditions.text: After the prefetch command, the benchmark runs with networking blocked and passes; a test asserts the telemetry-off environment variables are set before the runtime is imported.

claims.text: The resident models live in the per-user nvsh daemon, loaded on first use rather than at daemon start, and unloaded after an idle period; the one-shot client path asks the daemon rather than loading a model per call, and falls straight through to the full agent when the daemon is unavailable.

honesty_conditions.text: Daemon memory is measured before first tier use, while resident, and after the idle unload, on each device; a request made with the daemon stopped reaches the full agent without loading a model in the client.

claims.text: Each tier is reachable explicitly as a registered adapter (`@needle`, `@lfm`, `nvsh --agent needle`) as soon as its flavor is installed, is excluded from `nvsh setup`'s default-agent probe, and is reported by `nvsh agent list --json` and `nvsh doctor`. Automatic tier routing is off until the operator enables it in config. An explicit `@target` naming another harness always bypasses the tiers.

honesty_conditions.text: `@needle` and `@lfm` join the adapter conformance suite; a test asserts `nvsh setup`'s probe never offers them as the default agent, and that `@claude` sends a request past both tiers.

revisions.text: Each tier is also reachable explicitly as a registered adapter (`@needle`, `@lfm`, `nvsh --agent needle`) for testing and benchmarking, is excluded from `nvsh setup`'s default-agent probe, and is reported by `nvsh agent list --json` and `nvsh doctor`. An explicit `@target` naming another harness bypasses the tiers.

claims.text: Tier 2 runs a bounded loop: at most 4 inspection rounds, read-only operations only inside the loop, a bounded context, and three possible outcomes — propose an operation, explain the failure in plain text, or escalate. Escalation hands the full agent what Tier 2 already inspected so the work is not repeated.

honesty_conditions.text: A test with a fixture Tier 2 that never stops inspecting is cut off at 4 rounds and escalates; a mutating operation requested inside the loop is refused; the escalated request carries the inspection results.

claims.text: A repeatable benchmark corpus and runner are committed: the prompts and failure cases from issues #30 and #31, each with its expected operation, arguments or expected escalation. One command runs it on a device and writes a results file with accuracy, argument accuracy, false-mutating-pick count, escalation precision and recall, cold and warm latency, and resident and peak memory. Results for each device are committed under docs/.

honesty_conditions.text: Running the benchmark command twice on the same device and model gives the same accuracy numbers, and the results file records the model file hashes, nvsh version and device.

claims.text: No new auto-apply: every mutating action still needs operator approval, sudo and destructive-command rules are unchanged, and the local tiers only ever reach commands that the operation table can render. nvsh itself never sends measurement data off the machine; the only way records leave is a redacted export file the operator creates and moves by hand.

honesty_conditions.text: The existing approval, sudo and destructive-command tests pass unchanged with the tiers enabled, and a test asserts no tier code path opens a network socket other than to localhost.

revisions.text: No new auto-apply: every mutating action still needs operator approval, sudo and destructive-command rules are unchanged, and the local tiers only ever reach commands that the operation table can render. nvsh's own measurement data stays on the machine; nothing is sent off the box.
revisions.reason: q3 decision: local plus manual export

claims.text: Fine-tuning is not part of this spec. It establishes the baseline with stock Needle3 and post-trained LFM2.5 checkpoints and collects the data a fine-tune would need; training an LFM2.5 Base or a Needle LoRA with unsloth-cli or `needle finetune` is a follow-up decided from the committed benchmark results.

The tiers are not served through the lobes gateway, a remote model server, or a hosted API, and nvsh does not become a general tool-calling framework: the operation table is for machine operation on NVIDIA devices only.

On the committed corpus, on each benchmarked device: Tier 1 warm selection p95 < 150 ms; >= 90% of fast-path prompts get the correct operation and arguments; 0 wrong mutating operations proposed without the interpreted operation being shown; >= 80% of should-escalate prompts are declined by Tier 1; with both flavors resident the daemon adds < 1 GB to system memory on an Orin Nano; a command that succeeds still costs one bash function call and 0 forks.

honesty_conditions.text: Each number in the signal is produced by the committed benchmark command, not measured by hand; a missed target is reported as missed in the device's results file.

claims.text: One spec, delivered in phases: the operation table and observability first, then Tier 1 (Needle3), then Tier 2 (LFM2.5). Tier 2 may be dropped if its baseline fails.
Transparent routing is opt-in through config. Installing a flavor adds only the explicit `@needle` / `@lfm` targets; the operator switches on automatic tier routing once they have measured it.

Measurement records stay on the machine, and an operator-run export command bundles redacted records into a file for building fine-tune and benchmark data across the fleet. nvsh itself never sends data anywhere.

The Tier 2 model runtime is pluggable and chosen from benchmark evidence: the first implementation is a daemon-managed `llama-server` on localhost, and vLLM and SGLang must be selectable through the same OpenAI-compatible interface, because speed is the goal and the fastest runtime per device is not obvious.

Tier 2 talks to its model through one OpenAI-compatible localhost interface with tool-call support, and the runtime behind it is a config choice among `llama-server`, `vllm` and `sglang`: nvsh either starts and stops the runtime itself or attaches to one the operator already runs. The benchmark runner records speed and memory cost per runtime, so the default for each device class is picked from numbers, weighing footprint as heavily as latency.

honesty_conditions.text: The benchmark is run with at least two runtimes on at least one device and both result sets are committed; switching runtime is a config change with no code change, shown by a test that points Tier 2 at a fixture HTTP server.

revisions.text: Tier 2 talks to its model through one OpenAI-compatible localhost interface with tool-call support, and the runtime behind it is a config choice among `llama-server`, `vllm` and `sglang`: nvsh either starts and stops the runtime itself or attaches to one the operator already runs. The benchmark runner records results per runtime so the default for each device class is picked from numbers.
revisions.reason: operator: low memory impact; engines have different costs

claims.text: Low memory impact is a first-class goal alongside speed. Inference engines have different costs, so each runtime is judged on its whole resident footprint — engine process, weights, KV cache and any memory it reserves up front — and on its effect on the machine's primary workload, not on tokens per second alone.

honesty_conditions.text: For every runtime and device benchmarked, the results file records idle resident memory, peak memory during a turn, memory reserved at startup (vLLM and SGLang pre-allocate a share of GPU or unified memory) and the slowdown of a concurrent primary workload; the per-device default is the runtime that meets the latency target with the smallest footprint, and a runtime that cannot fit the Orin Nano budget is recorded as not fitting rather than left out.

open_vagueness.text: Whether stock LFM2.5-230M or 350M can do the Tier 2 role at all is unmeasured; the spike covered Needle3 only. If both fail and 1.2B also fails, Tier 2 is dropped and Tier 1 escalates straight to the full agent.
Needle3 has only been run on the DGX Spark. libneedle.so on the Jetsons' L4T userland (glibc version, tegra234 and tegra264) and on an 8 GB Orin Nano is unverified.
Fine-tuning Needle3 (LoRA) and an LFM2.5 Base checkpoint on nvsh data, using the records this spec starts collecting.
LFM Open License terms (attribution, commercial revenue threshold) need a read before nvsh documents or prefetches LFM2.5 weights; nvsh would download from the publisher, never redistribute.

scope_entries.finding: Asks for Needle3 as a local intent->typed-tool selector that never executes; selections become normal Proposals through nvsh approval/audit. Option A = explicit NvshAgent adapter (`@needle`), Option B = transparent router before backend selection (preferred end state). Device matrix Spark/AGX Thor/AGX Orin; the operator's request adds Orin Nano as an LLM-less/SLM-only target. Packaging must stay out of core deps (extra, external helper, or lazy import).

Tier 2 between Needle3 and the full agent: bounded 2-4 round inspect->interpret->propose loop over the same typed tool vocabulary, escalation as a first-class outcome. Sequencing is explicit: baseline post-trained LFM2.5-230M/350M (1.2B only if both fail) BEFORE any fine-tune of an LFM2.5 Base checkpoint with unsloth-cli. Objective is 'impact-less resident', not max tokens/sec; Orin Nano is the primary constrained target.

As read from the README/model card on 2026-09-19 (not yet run here): Apache-2.0; 121M params, 2-20 layer deployable subnetworks, 8-29 MB `.cact` files (2.125 bpw); `pip install cactus-needle` Python API, plus a <1 MB per-platform native `needle` binary with `--model --tools tools.json --prompt` and `--serve` (HTTP); Linux ARM64 listed. Output JSON carries `function_calls`, `reasoning` and a calibrated `confidence`; an uncovered request returns an empty list rather than a guess. LoRA fine-tune via `needle finetune` + `needle build --lora`. Unverified: max tool count, context length, latency on Jetson, CUDA vs CPU.

As read 2026-09-19 (not yet run here): text checkpoints at 230M, 350M, 1.2B, 2.6B; GGUF builds published (Q4_0..F16), so llama.cpp's OpenAI-compatible server can host them; LFM Open License carries attribution duties and a commercial revenue threshold — a licence nvsh would reference, not redistribute under.

Checked 2026-09-19 via the PyPI JSON API: one pure-Python wheel (py3-none-any, 90 KB), Apache-2.0, Python >=3.9, sole runtime dependency `huggingface_hub` (jax/flax only under the `train`/`gpu` extras). So the native engine and the `.cact` model are fetched at first use rather than shipped in the wheel — offline use needs an explicit prefetch step, and the dependency must stay outside nvsh's empty `dependencies` list.

Explored by qwen/worker, spot-checked by Claude: `dependencies = []` (pyproject.toml:16) and no `[project.optional-dependencies]` table exists yet, so an extra would be the repo's first; coverage gate `fail_under = 60`. scan-secrets only checks endpoints in JSON files and allows localhost/127.0.0.1/::1/0.0.0.0 (scripts/scan-secrets.py:189), so a committed localhost model-server URL passes. nvsh/installers.py only invokes apt-get/npm/snap and marks curl-pipe-sh steps `executable=False` — nvsh has no precedent for downloading a native binary or model weights itself. `PROBE_EXCLUDED = {openai-compat, demo}` (nvsh/agent/registry.py:59) is the existing way to keep an adapter out of `setup`'s probe. Adapter tests are named tests/test_agent_<name>.py and never need the real harness.

Explored by qwen/senses, spot-checked by Claude: the success path is 'one bash function call and nothing else — no fork, no Python import, no model call', so every tier must live behind the existing qualifying-failure / explicit-request boundary, never in the hook. The daemon's warm session belongs to the `default` target only; any other `Target` (`@claude/opus`, `/ask --agent fast`) runs one-shot in the client (docs/daemon.md:276, decision c25), and daemon failure also degrades to one-shot. A transparent router therefore has two entry paths to cover (daemon and one-shot client), and an explicit `@target` is an operator instruction the router must not intercept. Wire request = JSON line with shell, kind (failure/slash/explicit), version, request.target, context incl. redaction_report.

The typed tool vocabulary both issues assume does NOT exist. grep for device_info|gpu_stats|service_status|power_get|docker_list over nvsh/ returns 0 hits; `inspect-*`/`manage-*`/`rollback`/`verify` appear only as prose in CLAUDE.md and docs/architecture.md. `/power` and `/clocks` are `_stub_handler` stubs (nvsh/slash.py:523,529). Playbooks are four static per-platform markdown briefs looked up by platform kind, not failure->fix mappings. The nearest real structures are `ProposalKind` INSPECT/FIX/RETRY/VERIFY (nvsh/agent/base.py:41), `Proposal(command, rationale, kind)` whose command is a free shell string, and `nvsh/platform`'s `Value(name, text, source, method, present)` typed facts with provenance. So a typed operation table is new foundation work, and it is the precondition for both tiers.

An explicit `@needle` / `@lfm` adapter fits the existing contract: `AdapterSpec(name, binary, factory, description, path, hosted, needs_node)` in `ADAPTERS` (registry.py:196), a lazy-import `_make_<name>` factory, a `Capabilities` declaration (incl. `local_model`, `approval`, `unmediated_file_access`), and a row in tests/_fake_adapters.py + tests/test_agent_conformance.py. Constraints: adapter `__init__` must be cheap and spawn nothing (registry.py:311, capabilities are read by constructing the adapter); `PATH_VALUES` (registry.py:47) has no value for an in-process or helper-binary model; a reflex tier must join `PROBE_EXCLUDED` (registry.py:59) so `nvsh setup` never picks it as the default full agent; doctor's `check_agent_reachable` is an if/elif ladder on provider (nvsh/doctor_checks.py:818) where a new adapter lands in the 'no reachability probe' warning branch until given one.

Every agent turn passes through `client._stream_request` (nvsh/client.py:1774), fed by `handle_failure` (:1975), `ask` (:2066) and `_on_last_failure` (/fix, /explain). Warm vs one-shot is decided client-side by `_is_one_shot(target)` (:517) and mirrored by `Daemon._targeted` (nvsh/daemon.py:1389); the daemon-side equivalent hook is `Daemon.handle_message` (:1148) after `request_from_dict`. The `Target` rides inside the request JSON. A resident tiny model belongs in the per-user daemon (the only long-lived nvsh process); the one-shot client path has no warm process, so it would pay model load on every call unless it asks the daemon.

stdlib urllib SSE chat client, `tool_calling=False` (:274): it reads only `choices[0].delta.content` and ignores `tool_calls`. A llama.cpp server hosting an LFM2.5 GGUF on localhost is reachable TODAY via `[agents.openai-compat] base_url` — but only as a text explainer. The bounded inspect->interpret->propose loop of issue #31 needs tool-call parsing that no HTTP adapter in nvsh has yet.

`_VALID_TOP_KEYS = {agent, agents, aliases, sessions, triggers}` (:33) and unknown keys fail loudly, so a tier/router table is a schema change touching `_apply_*`, the `Config` dataclass, `_dump_toml` round-trip, `default_toml()` and docs/config.example.toml. `[agents.<name>]` keys are a closed set (provider, model, base_url, api_key_env, api_key_file, effort, extra_args, approval, fixture) — there is no key for a model file path or a confidence threshold today.

scope_entries.surface: Needle3 spike on DGX Spark (cactus-needle 3.0.2, untuned base, 10-tool nvsh vocabulary from issue #30)
scope_entries.finding: Run 2026-09-19 in a scratch venv, CPU, telemetry off. Warm selection 28-57 ms per request; import+load 5.7 s cold; process peak RSS 179 MB; engine is `libneedle.so` loaded via ctypes, engine+weights fetched from Hugging Face on first use. `Needle.complete()` selects only; `Needle.run()` EXECUTES the tool functions, so nvsh must never call `run()`. Accuracy on issue #30's prompts: 7/9 fast-path prompts correct with correct arguments (`power_set(mode=max_performance)`, `service_restart(service=vLLM)`); 2 wrong — 'How hot is this machine?' -> `power_get` at confidence 1.0, and 'Run nvsh doctor' -> `docker_restart(container=doctor)` at 0.66, a wrong MUTATING pick. Of 5 should-escalate prompts 3 returned an empty list; 'Figure out why CUDA initialization is failing' -> `device_info` at 0.98 and 'Fix this linker error' -> `nvsh_doctor` at 0.53. Conclusions: latency and footprint claims hold; confidence is NOT a safe gate on its own (a wrong pick scored 1.0); the package sets `confidence = None` for a fine-tuned model (needle/__init__.py, `if self._tuned`), so a tuned model has no confidence at all. Also: cactus-needle ships telemetry ON by default, posting an anonymous id, OS, arch, Python and engine version to a hosted endpoint on every `run`/`complete`; it is disabled by `NEEDLE_TELEMETRY=0` or `DO_NOT_TRACK`.
